items.summary: NVIDIA Dynamo introduces Shadow Engine Recovery, a feature that significantly reduces the time required to recover from LLM engine failures. When an engine process fails, the standard cold restart involves loading weights from storage, compiling kernels, and capturing CUDA graphs, which can take several minutes. Shadow Engine Recovery keeps a pre-initialized shadow engine idle on the same GPUs as the active engine, allowing it to take over almost instantly. The GPU Memory Service (GMS) enables weight sharing between engines without duplicating memory, ensuring the shadow engine can immediately resume serving. Testing showed that recovery time dropped from 283 seconds to 7.3 seconds, minimizing service disruption. The system uses a shared lock and GMS to manage memory and coordination between engines, enabling rapid failover. While the feature is in preview, it aims to improve reliability for large-scale LLM deployments.
items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo's Shadow Engine Recovery Reduces LLM Inference Outage Time

items.summary: Amazon and its vendors face challenges in optimizing supply chain operations due to information asymmetry. The work highlights the potential of mechanism design in supply chain coordination and opens new questions for future research.

items.summary: An autonomous agent was developed to address the issue of insufficient test coverage in large Rails monoliths. items.summary: Arvind Narayanan and Akash Kapur argue that AI companies are moving beyond model provision to higher stack layers to avoid the commodity trap. items.summary: The article argues that AI has not replaced software engineers and is unlikely to do so, despite widespread fears of job displacement. It examines the 'decide-execute-deliver' model of software development, noting that AI primarily automates the 'execute' phase but leaves the decision-making and delivery layers resistant to automation. The piece challenges narratives of AI-driven mass layoffs, citing examples like Block, Snap, and Intuit, where layoffs were often attributed to financial pressures or restructuring rather than AI. Surveys indicate that executives frequently cite AI as a reason for layoffs without evidence of actual implementation. The article also highlights that AI's productivity benefits are more evident in slower hiring rather than increased layoffs. While AI may reduce demand for certain roles, it does not eliminate the need for software engineers due to the complexity of decision-making and accountability. The authors conclude with cautious optimism, suggesting that the software engineering profession will continue to grow, albeit at a slower pace, as AI adoption progresses.
items.title: Software Engineering Jobs Remain Resilient Amid AI Adoption

items.summary: EDF and Centrica are nearing a £800m deal to extend Sizewell B's operating life to 2055, according to an EDF spokesperson. key_points: The study introduces a marginal cumulative multiplier to assess the impact of government spending and taxation on output during fiscal consolidations.

items.summary: A new study by Roberto Perotti and Luca Sala examines marginal tax and spending multipliers during fiscal consolidations in 16 countries from 1978 to 2020. The research introduces a marginal cumulative multiplier to measure the effect of government spending or taxation on output while holding the other fiscal instrument constant. The authors estimate a marginal spending multiplier of 1.5 and a marginal tax multiplier close to 0 in their benchmark analysis. Using the policy counterfactual method, they find spending multipliers never below 1.3 and tax multipliers no higher than -1. The study suggests existing literature's higher tax multipliers may result from improper scaling of fiscal variables.
items.title: Study finds spending multipliers higher than tax multipliers in fiscal consolidations

items.title: Owaisi criticizes RSS and BJP over Manusmriti opposition to Ambedkar's Constitution

items.summary: The government has exercised the full greenshoe option in the Hindustan Copper Offer for Sale (OFS), increasing the stake sale from 3% to 6%. This follows strong subscription of 3.41 times by non-retail investors on the first day of bidding. The OFS, open to retail investors on Wednesday, allows bids between 9:15 am and 3:30 pm on BSE and NSE. At least 10% of the OFS size is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares set aside for employees. The floor price of ₹514 per share, a discount to recent market prices, may not reflect the actual price retail investors face due to institutional demand. Analyst Vaqarjaved Khan notes the discount could disappear if institutional investors clear the OFS at higher prices. While the company's Q1 profit surged 163% year-on-year, improved margins are attributed to higher copper prices rather than operational improvements. Khan advises investors to consider the OFS for long-term copper exposure rather than short-term gains.
items.title: Government Exercises Greenshoe Option in Hindustan Copper OFS, Expanding Stake Sale to 6%

key_points: Demis Hassabis prioritizes scientific understanding over commercial metrics in AI development.

Hassabis's career reflects a blend of personal ambition and a quest to unlock the mysteries of intelligence.
items.summary: Sir Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and founder of DeepMind, emphasizes his scientific approach to AI, aiming to understand nature and the universe. His work at DeepMind focused on AI applications in medicine and agriculture rather than chasing user metrics. The book 'The Infinity Machine' explores his career, from his origins in North London to his role in developing breakthroughs like AlphaGo and AlphaFold. Hassabis's philosophy of deep reinforcement learning contrasts with early symbolic AI, allowing machines to learn through observation. The book also examines DeepMind's competitive landscape, including its response to OpenAI and the rise of Chinese AI labs like DeepSeek. It raises questions about the ethical implications of AI development and the challenges of managing its rapid growth.
items.title: Demis Hassabis's journey in AI and science

items.summary: NITI Aayog's report flags a structural imbalance in India's higher education system, where millions of students pursue generic degrees with weak job links. Only 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications, and 13% of all graduates are unemployed. The report notes that 1.86 crore students apply for just 55,000 government jobs, highlighting the mismatch between education and employment. It calls for reimagining higher education through industry participation and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models to align curricula with industry needs. The report suggests moving toward specialised, job-linked programmes and expanding work-integrated learning to improve employability.
items.title: NITI Aayog highlights job mismatch in India's higher education system

key_points: Tamil Nadu's CM C Joseph Vijay scrapped the Parandur site for Chennai's second airport, reversing a previous DMK government decision.

Current airport capacity is not yet at its limit, but experts warn of the long time required to develop a new airport and the risk of losing investment to other hubs.
Industry bodies urge the TVK government to expedite the search for an alternative site to avoid delays in infrastructure development.
The Parandur project was intended as long-term infrastructure, but the urgency of finding a new site remains due to the time needed for construction and clearances.
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has scrapped the Parandur site for Chennai's second airport, sending the project back to the drawing board. The decision, which the DMK's MK Stalin called an 'irreversible setback,' was made after protests from local communities concerned about displacement and environmental impact. While the existing Chennai International Airport has not yet reached its capacity threshold, experts warn that the long lead time for developing a new airport could delay necessary infrastructure. The airport's current capacity is expected to rise to 55 million passengers by 2026 with planned expansions, but industry bodies stress the urgency of finding an alternative site to avoid losing investment and talent to other regional hubs. The Parandur project, which would have handled 100 million passengers annually, was seen as long-term infrastructure rather than an immediate solution to congestion.
items.title: Chennai's Second Airport Project Back to Site Selection After Parandur Scrapped

items.summary: A study on the shola sky islands in the Western Ghats reveals how land use changes have impacted bird movements. Both forest and grassland species avoid human-dominated landscapes, but forest specialists face fewer movement obstacles in invaded woodlands. The Nilgiri pipit, the only grassland specialist in the study, experienced the most adverse effects from woody invasions and human activities. Between 1973 and 2017, the islands lost 516 sq km of grasslands and 63 sq km of forests. Researchers built 126 models to predict species movement patterns, finding that increased woodland cover fragmented grassland habitats, reducing connectivity for grassland species. The study highlights the need to restore native grasslands in the Shola Sky Islands to preserve biodiversity.

items.summary: The 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI) ranks India among the worst climate performers, sparking debate over fairness and ethical principles in climate rankings. Different indices, such as the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), yield conflicting results due to varying ethical frameworks. The EPI focuses on absolute greenhouse gas emissions, while the CCPI emphasizes per capita emissions, reflecting differing views on equity. A 2024 study shows that adjusting the EPI to incorporate fairness-based metrics significantly improves rankings for the Global South. The article argues that no single index is neutral, and policymakers should consider multiple indices to form a principled stance. Thailand's engagement with the EPI led to improved rankings, illustrating the value of constructive responses over rejection. The piece concludes that climate indices should be transparent about their design choices, and countries should use them to inform policy rather than dismiss them outright.
items.title: India's Climate Rankings Differ Across Indices Due to Ethical Premises
